newsitem.title: UK: Prompt N.Sea market heads up but Iraq barrels loom.
newsitem.headline: Prompt N.Sea market heads up but Iraq barrels loom.

text.p: The North Sea wet crude market fell silent on Thursday afternoon, but the value of benchmark Dated Brent looked set to at least hold its ground as the front month spread widened its backwardation.
August/September Brent traded at +20 cents two cents up on a deal done on Thursday. But September/October slipped slightly to trade at -5 cents.
Short-term fundamentals in the North Sea market were strong, traders said, with active trade on the first half August cargoes and attention already on the third decade for some non-Brent grades.
No Brents from the August loading programme have so far been "clocked" or left unclaimed at five o'clock on the day they turn wet.
"Within a narrow time horizon it's a fairly well supported, but you've always got the Iraq factor lurking in the background," said one trader.

A Brent cargo due to load Aug 13-15 traded at Aug Brent +6 cents to a Wall Street trader before midday, in line with the price fetched by an Aug 11-13 loader on Wednesday. Later a cargo with the same loading dates was heard offered by a U.S. refiner at Aug Brent +8 cents.
Brent short term swaps, or CFDs, gained a few cents across the board, with next week (Aug 4-8) heard traded at September +10 cents.

But outright levels slumped, dragged down by a burst of long liquidation on the August NYMEX gasoline contract ahead of its expiry at the close of trade. Firm gasoline prices due to tight U.S. supplies have been the key market driver over the last week.
September Brent was trading 36 cents down at $18.61 a barrel on the IPE at 1733 GMT.
Traders were still preoccupied with trying to second guess the timetable for the resumption of Iraqi exports.
The U.N. is expected to complete its review of Baghdad's aid distribution plan this week, but some traders remained sceptical that Iraq had any intention of resuming exports quickly.
Nevertheless, shipping brokers reported U.S. trader Bayoil was seeking to fix Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) to take Iraqi crude oil from the port of Mina al-Bakr around the middle of August.
Two Oseberg cargoes traded early on at Dated Brent +23 cents and a third at +26 cents, down from previously talked levels around +30 cents.

Meanwhile, Statoil said it had adjusted the August loading programme for Statfjord crude oil due to unscheduled shutdowns at the Statfjord C and Snorre platforms and generally lower-than-forecast production at the field.
Traders said August liftings had been put back by three days and two of the originally scheduled 28 cargoes had been deferred to September.
